criteria.criterion: Cold load: procedural texture generation starts at prefetch time (Play hover or focus) without blocking the hero (no main-thread task over 50 ms attributable to it while the hero is idle), and a cold-cache A/B on the production build at 1440x900 shows time from Play to playable reduced by most of the recorded 1.1 s; the cold-entry hero gap is re-measured on a quiet host (load average recorded) with no freeze over 50 ms.
criteria.evidence: Cold-cache A/B, production build in a copy, fresh Chrome profile per run, 1440x900, real GPU, 3 alternating runs each, host load 27-43 (NOT quiet), medians. Play click to swap into the game (first 'game' phase): no prefetch (cold click) 1311 -> 709 ms (-602 ms, 53% of the recorded 1.1 s); pointerdown+80 ms press 1086 -> 720 ms (-366); hover 600 ms then click 703 -> 395 ms (-308; baseline already pre-warmed on hover, new build is at the 360 ms chrome-exit floor). Play click to playable (Game started announce, includes the 1.5 s entry): cold 2849 -> 2245, press 2622 -> 2244, hover 2240 -> 1928. Cause: world textures are now painted in 3 workers (OffscreenCanvas, ImageBitmap) and started by Play hover, focus AND press (previously hover/focus on a fine pointer only, on the main thread, 710-750 ms); the shader warm-up links its programs in parallel (warm total 405 -> 210 ms). Hero idle after hover (6 s, no click, 2 runs per build): 0 long tasks (>50 ms) and 0 rAF gaps over 40 ms on both builds; world resources 715-730 ms -> 250-270 ms. Cold-entry hero gap (gl.render gaps before the swap, entry.mjs, 3 runs): 24, 27, 28 ms cold and 23, 27, 22 ms hover; gap into the first game frame 28-41 ms; all under 50 ms, at load average 28-32 (1 min). LIMITS: the host was never quiet (load 16-47 during all runs), 'most of 1.1 s' is met only narrowly on the cold click (53%) and not on press (33%) or hover (28%, the hover baseline had only about 310 ms left to save); programs compiled in the first 30 game frames is 2 in both builds (pre-existing, M4 report). Evidence: ab-all.log, ab-all-prelim.log, h/out/ab-*.json, h/out/entry-*.json m-final-*.json, final.log.

Bytes: additional first-play transfer after hover until ready = 944,993 B gzip (0.90 MiB: game chunks 830 kB, public/game clips 114 kB, worker chunk 3 x 2.5 kB not shown by the page's network target); worst case with the 1.9 MB dance.glb (850 kB gzip, normally already fetched by the hero) about 1.8 MB; target 8 MB MET. assumptions: The 1.1 s recorded in report 23 is compared against the A/B of this stage (baseline build = M4 HEAD 9847be9 in a copy); the old M2 floor was not rebuilt.
'Playable' is reported twice: the swap into the game (first game phase) and the Game started announce, which includes the fixed 1.5 s entry.
Headless Chrome rAF is vsync-capped at 60 Hz, so frame-time rows show headroom through the added render CPU time (gl.render wall time) rather than uncapped fps.
Phone numbers are emulation on this Mac's GPU (DPR 3 requested, the game caps at 2), not a physical device.

WebGL unavailable is produced with --disable-3d-apis; the shipped hero also fell over there before this stage, so hiding the Canvas and the Play button is the minimal fix, the voice talk button stays.
The page behind the game is defined as every sibling on the path from the stage to the body plus the hero chrome; the stage (canvas, loading strip, dialogs, game overlay) stays live.
Tab out of the page pauses the game (existing blur rule); the Tab sweep resumes it between steps.
decisionsProposed: Texture painting runs in up to 3 module workers with an ImageBitmap hand-off, with the main-thread paced painter as the automatic fallback (no Worker, no OffscreenCanvas, error, 20 s timeout); started by prepareWorld on every Play prefetch trigger.
The shader warm-up starts every unit's colour compile first and awaits the links together; a larger per-frame budget after the click was tried (hero gap up to 72 ms under load) and dropped.
Page-behind-the-game inert handling lives in shell/pageInert.ts and is applied and released by the shell with the scroll lock.
Without WebGL the hero renders no Canvas and no Play button (design 3.5 row).
lessonsProposed: Measure the failure rows in the real browser early: the 'WebGL unavailable' row looked implemented (a disabled Play button) but the hero Canvas threw and blanked the whole page.

A hover-prewarmed baseline hides most of a cold-load cost: A/B the no-prefetch click, the press and the hover separately, and report the click-to-swap phase as well as click-to-playable (the 1.5 s entry is common to both).
Waiting for each shader link before starting the next serialises the GPU process: start all compiles, await the links together, then read the program layouts.
A larger per-frame warm-up budget shortened the load but produced 72 ms hero gaps under host load 40; keep gap budgets to one program per frame.
In zsh, `for x in ...; do echo == $x` fails ('= not found') and `set -- $var` does not split words: quote the string or use ${=var}.
